title: FlowTrace agentic plugin system: agent research, artifact writing, validation, Neovim navigation, and contextual chat

node-overview.label: The agentic plugin system has three layers: Agent Skill, CLI, and Neovim plugin
node-overview.summary: The Agent Skill (SKILL.md) tells coding agents how to research and write .flow.json artifacts. The CLI provides deterministic validation, build scaffolding, context search, and terminal preview. The Neovim plugin loads artifacts into an interactive tree with jump, preview, details, and agent chat.

skill-skill.label: SKILL.md: the agent skill that orchestrates artifact creation
skill-skill.summary: The Agent Skills spec directory. SKILL.md contains frontmatter (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata) plus instructions telling coding agents to research code themselves first, then write .flow.json, then validate with the CLI.

skill-core-principle.label: Core principle: the agent builds understanding, FlowTrace is only the artifact format
skill-core-principle.summary: The skill instructs agents NOT to start by calling the FlowTrace CLI to explore. Instead, agents use their own code-reading tools, then write the artifact, then validate and print with the CLI. The CLI never calls LLMs.

skill-workflow.label: Skill workflow: confirm → research → organize → write → validate → print → open
skill-workflow.summary: Nine-step workflow: (1) confirm repo root and flow to trace, (2) ensure CLI available, (3) research codebase with own tools, (4) decide walkthrough structure, (5) write .flow.json, (6) validate, (7) print/preview, (8) fix issues and re-validate, (9) tell user how to open in Neovim.

cli-main.label: CLI entrypoint: main() dispatches build / context / validate / print
cli-main.summary: Tiny Go entrypoint. Requires at least one arg, then a switch on os.Args[1] picks the subcommand. Errors bubble up and exit non-zero. Four real commands plus help.

cli-dispatch.label: Subcommand switch: build / context / validate / print
cli-dispatch.summary: Each runX function parses its own flag.NewFlagSet and calls into the core package. build and context share core.Build; context sets DryRun=true.

cli-build.label: runBuild parses flags and calls core.Build
cli-build.summary: Reads --root, --out, --max-files, --max-nodes, --dry-run plus the request string, then hands BuildOptions to core.Build.

cli-context.label: runContext is core.Build with DryRun=true
cli-context.summary: Same code path as build, but DryRun=true short-circuits before any artifact is written. Outputs candidate snippets for an agent to read.

cli-validate.label: runValidate loads a .flow.json and validates it
cli-validate.summary: Two steps only: core.LoadFlow then core.ValidateFlow against --root. Returns error if any check fails.

cli-print.label: runPrint loads a .flow.json and renders the tree to stdout
cli-print.summary: core.LoadFlow then core.PrintFlow(os.Stdout, flow). No validation; just walks and prints.

core-build.label: core.Build: tokenize → search → scaffold → normalize → validate → write
core-build.summary: Heart of the build pipeline. Tokenizes the request, walks the repo for candidate hits, formats snippets (and exits if DryRun), otherwise builds a heuristic Flow, normalizes it, validates it, and writes the JSON.

request-terms.label: requestTerms tokenizes the natural-language request into search terms
request-terms.summary: Lowercases, splits on word chars, drops a small stopword set and tokens shorter than 3 chars. Returns a deduped slice used by searchRepo.

search-repo.label: searchRepo walks the repo scoring candidate files by term matches
search-repo.anchor: func searchRepo(root string, terms []string, max int)
search-repo.summary: filepath.WalkDir, skipping .git/.flowtrace/node_modules/vendor/dist/build/target. For each text-source file: +1 per matching line (stores up to 8), +3 per term that hits the relative path. Sorts by score desc and trims to max.

format-snippets.label: formatSnippets prints markdown-ish score/match blocks for the agent
format-snippets.summary: Markdown-ish dump of each candidate file plus its matched lines. This is the entire output of the context subcommand. The agent reads these as hints, not as a final artifact.

heuristic-flow.label: heuristicFlow scaffolds a linear Flow from the top-scoring candidates
heuristic-flow.summary: Greedy: each candidate becomes one node-N in score order, chained as parent→child. Resolution is set to search. Fallback emits a single placeholder pointing at README.md if no candidates matched.

normalize.label: normalizeAndResolve fixes paths, defaults, and stale file references
normalize.summary: Cleans file paths, defaults Column to 1, defaults Resolution to llm_inferred, and if a node's file doesn't exist it tries to remap by basename to a known candidate.

schema-flow.label: Schema: Flow and FlowNode structs define the .flow.json shape
schema-flow.summary: Flow has schemaVersion, id, title, createdAt, root, and a nodes map. FlowNode has id, label, kind, file, line, column, summary, symbol, anchor, resolution, children, branches, and alternatives. Branch targets and child IDs must reference other nodes in the map.

validate-flow.label: ValidateFlow checks schema, files, line ranges, child/branch references
validate-flow.summary: Required fields: id, title, root. Every node must have label, kind, file, line≥1, valid resolution (lsp/ast/search/llm_inferred/llm_validated/manual). Files must exist under root, lines must be within range, children and branch targets must exist in the nodes map.

count-lines.label: countLines reads a file and counts newlines for line-range validation
count-lines.summary: Used by ValidateFlow to ensure node.Line never exceeds the file length. Empty files return 1.

load-flow.label: LoadFlow reads and json.Unmarshals into *Flow
load-flow.summary: Single source of truth for parsing. Both validate and print go through this.

write-flow.label: WriteFlow marshals indented JSON and writes the artifact
write-flow.summary: json.MarshalIndent with two-space indent plus trailing newline. The output path defaults to .flowtrace/<slug>.flow.json if --out is empty.

print-flow.label: PrintFlow writes the title then recurses from the root
print-flow.summary: Maintains a seen map so cycles or shared subtrees print once and then say ↳ already shown.

print-node.label: printNode draws └─/├─ tree connectors per node, then children, then branches
print-node.anchor: func printNode(w io.Writer, f *Flow, id, prefix string
print-node.summary: Recursive. Branches are rendered after children with a branch: label so they read as alternative paths in the tree.

nvim-plugin-entry.label: plugin/flowtrace.lua: registers :FlowTrace* user commands on first load
nvim-plugin-entry.summary: Guard-loads once per session via vim.g.loaded_flowtrace. Registers nine user commands: FlowTraceOpen, Last, Next, Prev, Close, Refresh, Ask, AskFlow, Chat, ChatClear, and AgentProvider. Each is a thin wrapper that lazy-requires the flowtrace module.

nvim-init.label: init.lua: setup, state, keymaps, redraw, and public API
nvim-init.summary: Central module. Holds shared state (flow, expanded, index, agent_chat, config). M.setup merges agent config. M.open loads the artifact, renders the tree, and wires keymaps. M.last/next/prev cycle .flowtrace/*.flow.json files. M.refresh re-parses. M.close/M.ask/M.ask_flow/M.chat/M.chat_clear/M.agent_provider expose the public API.

nvim-setup.label: M.setup merges agent/provider config into state
nvim-setup.summary: Accepts opts.agent with optional providers table. Each provider is deep-extended with agent.defaults(). Stores providers in state.config.agent_providers, selects the default provider by name, and falls back to the first sorted provider. If opts.agent is a plain table (no providers key), it's merged as a single unnamed config.

agent-defaults.label: agent.defaults() returns the standard agent command template
agent-defaults.summary: Default config: command='pi', args={'-p'}, prompt_arg='Answer the user\'s FlowTrace question using the context from stdin.', timeout_ms=60000, max_chat_turns=6. Every provider is deep-extended over these defaults.

cmd-agent-provider.label: :FlowTraceAgentProvider switches or shows the chat agent provider
cmd-agent-provider.summary: With no arg, shows the current provider name and available names. With an arg, calls M.agent_provider to switch state.config.agent to the named provider. Provides tab completion from agent_provider_names().

nvim-open.label: M.open: load → side window → setup highlights → keymaps → redraw
nvim-open.summary: Captures the current window as state.source_win (so jumps know where to land), calls parser.load, creates the side panel, wires keymaps, and draws the tree.

parser-load.label: parser.load reads the JSON file, decodes it, and checks root/nodes
parser-load.summary: Uses vim.fn.readfile then vim.json.decode. Validates that the result is a table with a nodes table and a root key. Errors are raised, not returned.

window-open.label: window.open_buffer creates the left-side scratch buffer and vertical split
window-open.summary: topleft vertical Nnew at ~42% width. Sets buftype=nofile, bufhidden=wipe, swapfile=false, filetype=flowtrace, plus wrap/linebreak/cursorline/no numbers.

setup-highlights.label: setup_highlights defines FlowTrace* highlight groups with explicit colors
setup-highlights.summary: Defines FlowTraceTitle, FlowTraceHelp, FlowTraceLabel, FlowTraceMarker, FlowTraceBranch, FlowTraceMeta, FlowTraceFile, and FlowTraceSummary with Catppuccin-inspired explicit colors (rather than linking to theme groups that might be too flat).

nvim-setup-keys.label: setup_keys binds <CR>/a/A/C/p/f/F/?/o/q/r in the tree buffer
nvim-setup-keys.summary: Buffer-local normal-mode mappings. <CR>→jump, a→ask_node, A→ask_flow, C→clear_chat, p→preview, f→next flow, F→prev flow, ?→details, o→toggle expanded+redraw, q→close, r→refresh.

nvim-toggle.label: o toggles state.expanded for the current node and redraws
nvim-toggle.summary: Looks up the current row's node id from state.index, flips its expansion boolean, and calls redraw().

nvim-redraw.label: redraw renders lines + extmark highlights into the tree buffer
nvim-redraw.summary: Calls tree.render(flow, expanded), replaces buffer lines, clears the FlowTrace namespace, then re-applies highlights as extmarks. Buffer is flipped non-modifiable around the writes.

tree-render.label: tree.render builds the lines/index/highlights triple for display
tree-render.summary: Emits a title line, help line, blank line, then recursively walks from flow.root. Returns lines (for buffer content), index (row→{id, node} for cursor lookup), and highlights (row/col/extmark metadata for coloring).

tree-add-node.label: add_node recursively emits label + meta + file + summary rows per node
tree-add-node.summary: Per node: a marker line with ▾/▸ icon, ↳ branch label, file:line location. Then indented annotation lines for label, metadata (kind and resolution source), and summary. Uses a seen map to prevent infinite recursion (prints 'already shown' instead).

action-jump.label: actions.jump opens the node's file and positions the cursor
action-jump.summary: Picks a code window (or creates one), :edits the file, resolves location via anchor→symbol→line fallback, sets the cursor, and centers with zz. Leaves the tree window open.

code-window.label: code_window picks (or creates) a non-FlowTrace window for jumps
code-window.summary: Tries state.source_win first, then any other window whose buffer isn't a sidebar/picker/help/qf/flowtrace buffer. As a last resort splits a rightbelow vertical new.

resolve-location.label: resolve_location matches anchor → symbol → falls back to node.line
resolve-location.summary: find_in_buffer first does a plain substring match on node.anchor, then a whitespace-tolerant regex retry. Falls back to node.symbol with the same two-pass strategy. Finally falls back to node.line. This is why anchors survive minor source edits.

action-details.label: actions.details opens a floating markdown window with node metadata
action-details.summary: Builds a small markdown buffer (label, kind, file:line, anchor, symbol, resolution, summary) and shows it as a centered floating window. q or <Esc> closes it.

agent-ask-node.label: agent.ask_node opens chat scoped to the current node
agent-ask-node.summary: Convenience entry that calls ask(state, 'current-node'). Opens the floating chat panel with current-node scope.

agent-ask-flow.label: agent.ask_flow opens chat scoped to the whole flow
agent-ask-flow.summary: Convenience entry that calls ask(state, 'whole-flow'). Opens the floating chat panel withwhole-flow scope, which includes the full outline and all summaries.

agent-chat-window.label: M.show_chat creates/reuses a floating markdown chat window
agent-chat-window.summary: Creates a floating buffer with filetype=markdown, maps q/<Esc> to close, <CR> to submit, i/a/o to enter insert. Creates a floating window with rounded border and centered position. Calls render_chat to populate current conversation, then focuses the input line.

agent-submit.label: submit_question extracts the question, builds the prompt, and calls agent.run
agent-submit.summary: Reads the > input line, trims it, appends user+assistant(Thinking...) to agent_chat, sets agent_busy, renders the chat, then calls M.run with the full prompt. On callback, replaces Thinking... with the real answer and re-renders.

agent-build-prompt.label: M.build_prompt assembles context: rules, question, scope, node, source, outline, chat
agent-build-prompt.summary: Builds a structured markdown prompt with: system instructions (concise, grounded, no file modifications), the user question, current scope, flow title/id/artifact path, current node details (label, type, file, anchor, symbol, summary, children, branches), nearby source (±30 lines with line numbers), flow outline, and recent chat transcript (last max_chat_turns exchanges).

agent-node-section.label: node_section formats the current node's fields for the prompt
agent-node-section.summary: Formats ID, label, type, file:line, anchor, symbol, summary, children list, and branches list into a structured text block for inclusion in the prompt.

agent-nearby-source.label: nearby_source reads ±30 lines around the resolved location
agent-nearby-source.summary: Reads the node's source file with vim.fn.readfile, resolves the line using anchor→symbol→line fallback (same as jump), then extracts ±30 lines with line-numbered formatting.

agent-flow-outline.label: flow_outline recursively traces the node graph into a readable tree
agent-flow-outline.summary: Renders the full node graph as indented text with label, kind, file:line for each node. Uses a seen map to prevent infinite recursion. Included in the prompt so the agent understands the overall walkthrough structure.

agent-transcript.label: recent_transcript returns the last N turns of the chat history
agent-transcript.summary: Extracts up to max_chat_turns * 2 messages from state.agent_chat, formatted as 'User: ...' / 'Assistant: ...'. Gives follow-up continuity even when the external command is stateless.

agent-run.label: M.run executes the external agent command with stdin and timeout
agent-run.summary: Builds a command array from config.command + config.args + config.prompt_arg. Sends the prompt as stdin. Uses vim.system when available (Neovim 0.10+), falling back to vim.fn.jobstart with stdin piping. Implements a UV timer for timeout_ms. On success, calls callback(true, stdout). On failure or timeout, calls callback(false, error_message).

agent-clear-chat.label: agent.clear_chat resets the in-memory transcript and re-renders
agent-clear-chat.summary: Sets state.agent_chat = {}, calls render_chat, and notifies. Used to start a fresh conversation without closing the window.

nvim-last.label: M.last globs .flowtrace/*.flow.json and opens the most recently modified one
nvim-last.summary: Uses vim.fn.glob to list .flowtrace/*.flow.json, sorts by mtime (via vim.uv.fs_stat), and calls M.open with the latest file.

nvim-refresh.label: M.refresh re-parses state.path and redraws the tree
nvim-refresh.summary: No-op if no path has been opened. Reuses the existing tree buffer/window and the current state.expanded map.
